svg.text: Operational product · NASA/JPL OPERA · exact rules
OPERA DSWx-S1: the exact rules, checked on Warren County data
Rules and numbers from the open-source code (opera-adt/DSWX-SAR, commit d9ae8ed, Mar 2026). Examples: Sentinel-1, 17 Feb 2025, Bowling Green.
A
Inputs, and how slope is computed
• γ⁰ VV and γ⁰ VH: OPERA RTC-S1, 30 m; Bregman total-variation filter (λ = 20), then dB
• o = JRC occurrence / 100 (0 = never water … 1 = always water)
• h = HAND from ASF GLO-30 (m); land cover: GLAD 2020 (or ESA WorldCover)
• slope θ from the 30 m DEM with a 3 × 3 Sobel filter (Sₓ shown, S_y = transpose):
then scored with Z(θ; 0.5°, 15°): flat ground looks water-like
(a 3 × 3 Sobel sums to 8 · Δz, so the usual divisor is 8 · 30 m)
Checked on Warren County's real 30 m DEM (USGS 3DEP):
median slope
2.9° standard (÷ 8·30 m)
7.8° OPERA as written
area steeper than 5°
30 % standard (÷ 8·30 m)
67 % OPERA as written
Synthetic check: a 5.7° plane comes out as 14.9°. Worth confirming with the OPERA team.
B
Thresholds: tiles → Kittler–Illingworth → map
0 dB
pixel count, √ scale
Real tile: VV backscatter in the 3
× 3 km around the Barren River
gauge, 17 Feb 2025. OPERA's KI
formula gives τ = -18.3 dB, water
peak -20.8 dB (VH: τ -27.1, peak
Tiles searched 400 → 200 → … → 40 px (step ½ window) until > 20 pass.
A tile is used only if ALL of:
1. it straddles JRC water: 0 < water fraction < 1 in the normal, flood (+16 px) or
drought (−10 px) version of the JRC mask, and ≥ ⅓ of its pixels are valid;
2. maxₜ P₁P₂(μ₁ − μ₂)² / σ² > 0.7 (dB histogram −30 … 5 dB, 100 bins);
3. two fitted Gaussians: 2 of {Ashman D > 1.5, bimodality > 0.7, Sarle > 5/9}
(or D > 3), and surface ratio min(A₁, A₂) / max(A₁, A₂) > 0.1.
τ = argminₜ [ P₁ ln σ₁ + P₂ ln σ₂ − P₁ ln P₁ − P₂ ln P₂ ]
bounds τ_VV ∈ [−28, −11] dB, τ_VH ∈ [−28, −18] dB; above the bound → 3-Gaussian fit
(each mode ≥ 8 % of the largest), keep the lower valley; humps that barely overlap →
τ placed between their 99th / 1st percentiles. Tile τ and μ_w are averaged and interpolated
(gdal_grid) into maps τ(x), μ_w(x) for VV and for VH. OPERA does not publish these maps.
C
Fuzzy logic: five scores → one number F per pixel
Z(v; a, b) = 1 if v ≤ a; 1 − 2((v−a)/(b−a))² if v ≤ (a+b)/2; 2((v−b)/(b−a))² if v < b; 0 if v ≥ b. S = 1 − Z
radar VV: Z(σ; μ_w, τ)
-10 dB
radar VH: Z(σ; μ_w, τ)
-16 dB
HAND: Z(h; 0, 15 m)
history: S(o; 0.80, 0.95)
F = ½ · mean(Z_VV, Z_VH) + ½ · (Z_HAND + Z_slope + S_history) / 3
Real pixel 0.24 km from the Barren River gauge, mapped OPEN WATER by OPERA on 17 Feb 2025 (red dots):
VV -18.6 dB, VH -22.9 dB, HAND 0.08 m, slope 6.0° (OPERA formula; 2.3° standard), JRC occurrence 0%
Terrain + history half (exact): ½ · (1.00 + 0.71 + 0.00) / 3 = 0.285
Radar half with THIS tile's τ, μ_w: ½ · (0.04 + 0.00) / 2 = 0.010 → F = 0.29 (below 0.51 → not water here)
OPERA still mapped it as water, so its interpolated local τ at this pixel must be higher than this single tile's: the threshold map, not one tile, decides.
Polarisation swaps before averaging (where one polarisation is known to mislead):
• VH score ← VV score where water comes and goes (0.1 < o < 0.9) and VH < −18 dB, or on flat dry-looking land
(bare / shrubs / grassland / herbaceous wetland, θ < 5°, VH < −18 dB): VH cannot tell smooth dry land from water there;
• VV score ← VH score where water is permanent (o ≥ 0.9) and VH < −24 dB: wind roughens open water in VV, not in VH;
• HAND > 200 m → F = 0. Radar and terrain/history each carry exactly half of F.
D
Sure seeds and region growing
seed: F > 0.81
grow: add 4-neighbours with F > 0.51,
repeat until no pixel is added (no limit)
radar score needed
JRC history o (0 = never water, 1 = always)
to be a seed: 0.95 at o = 0
to be grown in: 0.35 at o = 0
max possible = 1
HAND = 0
• Terrain + history can give at most 0.50 < 0.51: no pixel becomes water without radar evidence.
• Ground that was never water (o = 0) can be a seed only if the mean radar score > 0.95;
so new flood mostly enters by growing outward from seeds in or near the river.
• The real pixel in C: terrain + history = 0.285, so a seed would need a radar score of 1.05 (impossible);
it can only be grown in, with a mean radar score > 0.45.
E
Dark land, edge check, water under vegetation
Dark land → not water if ALL:
land cover ∈ {bare/sparse vegetation, urban, moss & lichen} (+ grassland, shrubs),
o < 0.05, VV < −14.6 dB and VH < −22.8 dB; except within 3 px of JRC occurrence ≥ 0.10.
Edge check, per water object ≥ 40 px:
the object and its surroundings must pass the same two-Gaussian test as the tiles.
Water under vegetation:
r = 10 log₁₀( Lee₃ₓ₃[ γ⁰_VV / γ⁰_VH ] )
flooded vegetation if r > 8 dB and VH > −26 dB and land cover ∈ GLAD classes
19–24, 112–124, 125–148, 200–207 (with WorldCover: herbaceous wetland).
OPERA 'flooded vegetation', 17 Feb
2,930 pixels: our VV − VH
median VH -18.1 dB · fits r > 8 dB
dark pixel, 17 Feb (OPERA: not water)
r = 14.1 dB, but VH ≤ −26 dB
→ not flooded vegetation ✓
Caution from the same data: the flooded-vegetation pixel nearest the gauge carries that
label on the dry reference date (24 Jan 2025) too, so the ratio rule can flag vegetation
that is not flooded.
Numbers are DSWX-SAR defaults; the Warren County DSWx-S1 tiles list the same fuzzy ranges in their metadata. Several defaults differ from the 2024 ATBD (seeds 0.81 vs 0.8, growth 0.51 vs 0.6,
dark land −14.6 / −22.8 vs −13.4 / −22.2 dB). Examples computed by scripts/t1_opera_rules_check.py from open data; OPERA's own τ maps and F are not published.
